narrative.overview: The Platform is the whole project: PostgreSQL as the identity and authorization system, the relay that carries bytes, the CLI that installs and hardens, and the studio — the interface a reader works in. The studio is a working surface, not a canvas: light and dense on purpose, with a near-black module bar, a navigation pane that names the workspace in view, a sticky header carrying the page’s actions, and the page itself. Its character comes from what it shows rather than how it decorates: every right in PostgreSQL’s own privilege names with one full / half / empty mark, every change showing its SQL before it runs, every withheld field or filtered row saying why. Interface text is Inter; anything the database owns is JetBrains Mono, so the reader can always tell the studio’s voice from the database’s. Depth is mostly flat: hairlines and three tonal greys separate regions, and shadows are reserved for things that float.
keyCharacteristics: Light frame: paper content, the palette’s neutral greys, a near-black module bar.
One orange primary, for action and selection, and nowhere else.
Inter for the interface; JetBrains Mono for everything the database owns.
Rights drawn as PostgreSQL privilege names with full / half / empty marks, and a legend beside.
The statement is shown before the change runs.
Unboxed sections; a card is the only box.
A pinned palette of sixteen families, eleven of them reserved for an item’s own colour.

rules.name: The One Orange Rule
rules.body: Orange means "do this" or "this is chosen". It never decorates a heading, a border at rest, or an empty state; if an element is neither an action nor a selection (nor a held privilege), it is grey or blue.

rules.name: The Bright Fill Rule
rules.body: A family’s bright step fills; its dark step carries the text and the small marks that sit on light grounds. Orange fills with the palette’s black for its label.

rules.name: The Action-and-Information Rule
rules.body: Orange is what the reader can act on; blue is what the system is telling them. A notice, a policy statement or a row-security state is blue, even where an orange badge calls out what applies to you inside it.

rules.name: The Palette-Only Rule
rules.body: No colour enters the interface that the pinned palette does not hold — in the chrome as well as in the data.

rules.name: The Word-Meaning Tone Rule
rules.body: A listed value’s badge colour follows what the word means, not its position in the list: settled words are green, ended or refused words are red, in-progress words are amber, starting words are grey, and anything else is blue. The accent never takes a value’s tone.

rules.name: The Item Colour Rule
rules.body: A workspace or a collection may carry a colour of its own, stored with its metadata. The colour fills that item’s mark and nowhere else: never a heading, never a border, never a ground, and never the accent.

rules.name: The Database Speaks Mono Rule
rules.body: If PostgreSQL owns the text (a value, a name, a privilege, a statement), it is set in JetBrains Mono; if the studio wrote it, it is Inter.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface that sits in the page has no shadow; a surface that sits over the page has Float. A card, a panel and a sign-in step are in the page, and a shadow on any of them is a mistake.

rules.name: The Unboxed Section Rule
rules.body: A page section is a heading, a short description and a hairline above it; it is never a bordered box. A card is the only box on the page, so boxes never nest inside boxes.

rules.name: The Sticky First Column Rule
rules.body: In a record table the first field stays pinned while the rest scrolls, once there are more than three columns. A value longer than its column ends in an ellipsis at 320px, and the whole value is in its title.

rules.name: The One Rights Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: Rights are named only by PostgreSQL’s privileges (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE) and drawn only with the full / half / empty mark; never with checkmarks, toggles or invented role words.

rules.name: The Statement First Rule
rules.body: Nothing changes the database without its SQL on screen first, in the same view as the button that runs it.

dos: Do use Studio Orange only for actions, selection, focus and held privileges.
Do use Signal Blue only for what the system is telling the reader.
Do take every colour from the pinned palette, including the chrome.
Do set every database-owned string in JetBrains Mono and every studio-written string in Inter.
Do draw rights with PostgreSQL privilege names and the full / half / empty mark, with the legend nearby.
Do show the statement in a "Runs as you" figure before the button that runs it.
Do pin the first column of record tables, clip long values with an ellipsis, and keep the whole value in the title.
Do separate page sections with a heading and a hairline; let the card be the only box.
Do tone choice badges by what the word means.
Do let an item carry its own name, icon and colour, and draw them as its mark alone.
Do keep the frame light, sign-in included; the only dark surface is the module bar.
donts: Don't nest a bordered box inside a section box or a card inside a card.
Don't introduce a second accent hue or use orange decoratively.
Don't put a reserved family into the chrome while no categorical data asks for it.
Don't let an item's colour spread past its mark, or take the accent's place.
Don't describe rights with checkmarks, toggles or words other than PostgreSQL's privileges.
Don't run a change whose statement the reader has not been shown.
Don't colour choice badges by their position in the list.
Don't give an in-page surface a shadow; shadows are for floating layers and the primary action.
Don't return to a dark console frame.
Don't label an orange button in white: it is 3.4:1, where the palette's black on orange is 5.5:1.
